tori_cs: Heads up: new onboarding for 'Orchid' having a messy warmup. We see a mix of 401 auth failures and 429s during Node SDK ramp (~210 clients). Can infra advise quick mitigations?

orchid-dev: Paste of logs:
```
[2026-11-12T09:11:39Z] user=orch-01 auth=ok token_age=2s status=200 id=aa11
[2026-11-12T09:11:39Z] user=orch-02 auth=failed error=insufficient_quota
[2026-11-12T09:11:39Z] user=orch-03 status=429 message=\"rate limit exceeded\"
[2026-11-12T09:11:39Z] user=orch-04 auth=failed error=invalid_token (clock skew)
```
Init snippet they used:
```
const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.RW_KEY });
await client.preflight(); // called per tab/session open
```
They also mint ephemeral tokens per request in some flows.

devon_eng: Two issues colliding: preflight stampede + a few machines with clock skew causing intermittent invalid_token. Quick, high-impact fixes to push now: (1) stop preflight-per-tab; do process/session-level caching, (2) cache preflight for 40-60s, (3) add randomized splay before preflight calls during ramp, (4) switch to session-scoped ephemeral tokens instead of per-request, (5) ensure clients sync clock (NTP) to avoid invalid_token errors, (6) enable http2 keepalive / connection reuse.

tori_cs: Can you give a tiny copy-paste snippet we can send them? Keep it minimal.

devon_eng: Sure, send this pattern (Node):
```
// process-level cached preflight + jitter
let pf={ts:0,res:null};
async function cachedPreflight(){
  if(Date.now()-pf.ts < 50000) return pf.res; // 50s cache
  await new Promise(r=>setTimeout(r, Math.floor(Math.random()*300)+75));
  pf = {ts: Date.now(), res: await client.preflight()};
  return pf.res;
}
// use one ephemeral token per session and reuse connections (http2)
```
Also check system clock on any dev machines that consistently see invalid_token.

ops-bot: Alert: key=rw_live_**** observed onboarding-throttle at 2026-11-12T09:11:39Z. Window=120s peak_rps=66 avg_rps=17. Recommend reducing concurrent preflight to <=20 or request a short warmup quota for one-off ramps.

orchid-dev: We patched to cachedPreflight(50s), added 75-375ms splay and switched to session tokens. Ran a small canary: 429s dropped from ~33% sessions to ~2%, invalid_token errors went to 0 after clock sync.

tori_cs: Great. Follow-ups: (1) if they need to do a one-time warmup >20 concurrency, please open support with canary timestamps and we can grant a temporary 10m bump. (2) Capture token_age and source_ip in preflight logs for any future triage.

devon_eng: One more ops note: for customers expecting steady >60 rps, recommend Dedicated/reserved warmup. For transient ramps, client-side caching + splay + session tokens resolves most issues.

orchid-dev: Filing ticket now in support (will paste id). Thanks for the rapid help :thumbsup:
